investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC: curl of the task-given official events page (Nuxt-rendered HTML plus a JSON-LD ItemList and an embedded __NUXT_DATA__ SSR payload). Level 2 STRUCTURAL: decoded the __NUXT_DATA__ devalue payload to identify the public, self-documenting Hydra/API-Platform JSON API (/api/events) the Nuxt frontend itself calls, then fetched that API directly with the correct documented filter parameters.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.104.fr/programme?genre=concerts returned a Nuxt-rendered page with one JSON-LD block — an ItemList of 62 programme items (title + URL only, no dates/venue/price) — and an embedded __NUXT_DATA__ SSR payload (a devalue-encoded flat array) carrying a richer Hydra collection with full event records. However, the '?genre=concerts' query string was NOT honoured server-side: the embedded payload's own hydra:totalItems (62) and its sampled member list included non-music items (a market, workshops, a theatre piece) identically to an unfiltered fetch — confirming genre filtering happens client-side after hydration, not on this static response. The raw HTML/JSON-LD/SSR payload alone therefore cannot reliably isolate concerts from the venue's full multi-discipline programme (theatre, dance, exhibitions, workshops, markets) without further work.

Decoded the __NUXT_DATA__ payload's own devalue-encoded structure (a flat, index-referencing array, the same general encoding family as ingestion/sveltekit-data/decode.mjs already handles for SvelteKit, though Nuxt's own reactive-wrapper tags required a small variant resolver) and found it embeds a genuine Hydra (API Platform / Symfony) JSON-LD collection whose member resources carry their own '@id' (e.g. '/api/events/90') and 'name'/'arrayDates'/'placesNames'/'tags'/'minPrice'/'maxPrice'/'url' fields. Fetching that API directly at https://www.104.fr/api/events (Accept: application/ld+json, no authentication) confirmed it is public and fully self-documenting: its own 'hydra:search' IriTemplate lists every supported filter. Resolving the site's own 'Concert' tag IRI via GET /api/tags?search=concert (-> '/api/tags/14') and then querying /api/events with 'taggedEntities.tag[]=/api/tags/14', 'sortingFirstDateTime[after]=2026-08-26', and 'order[sortingFirstDateTime]=asc' correctly returned exactly the future, concert-tagged subset (22 items) with full structured fields — fully answering the investigation question. No further escalation was needed.

venue_reference: CENTQUATRE-PARIS ('Le 104') — multidisciplinary cultural venue, 5 rue Curial (public entrance) / 104 rue d'Aubervilliers, 75019 Paris

identity.notes: The retained page's own JSON-LD 'Organization' node ('@id': 'https://www.104.fr/#identity') directly states name 'Le Centquatre-Paris' and address streetAddress '5 Rue Curial', postalCode '75019', addressLocality 'Paris' — an exact match to the task-given public-entrance address. Every sampled API record's own 'placesNames' field additionally states 'Le CENTQUATRE-PARIS' directly.

site_classification.platform: Nuxt 3 (SSR, confirmed via '__NUXT__'/__NUXT_DATA__ markers and /_nuxt/ asset paths) frontend over a Symfony/API-Platform backend exposing a public Hydra JSON-LD REST API at /api/*. The Nuxt frontend's own SSR payload embeds calls to this same API; fetching it directly (bypassing the Nuxt page entirely) is the clean, structured, documented acquisition path — exactly the 'JSON data endpoint the Nuxt frontend itself calls' the task brief anticipated.

title.notes: Each API event resource's own 'name' field, stated directly.

start_date.notes: Each API event resource's own 'arrayDates[0]', a full ISO 8601 instant with explicit UTC offset (e.g. '2026-11-27T20:30:00+01:00'), stated directly. 'sortingFirstDateTime' independently repeats the same value for sorting purposes.

time.notes: The same 'arrayDates[0]' string carries an explicit numeric UTC offset — a confirmed UTC instant, not a floating local guess.

end.notes: Each single-performance API event resource's own 'arrayDates[1]' is a full ISO 8601 end instant with the same explicit offset, directly stated — confirmed to be a genuine performance end-time (not a multi-day span marker) by cross-checking 'longRunningEvent: false' on the same record.

venue_location.notes: This is a single-venue source: every API event resource's own 'placesNames' field directly states 'Le CENTQUATRE-PARIS', combined with the source's own separately-retained Organization address (identity evidence).

source_record_id.notes: Each API event resource's own '@id' (e.g. '/api/events/90') is the source's own Hydra/API-Platform resource IRI — a documented, stable, source-declared identity scheme (the API's own permanent resource path), not a guessed or hashed substitute. The numeric suffix is used as source_record_id.

event_url.notes: Each API event resource's own 'url' field (site-relative, e.g. '/fr/programmation/saison-2026-2027/concert/canine-liminal'), resolved against the venue's own domain.

price.value: 10.00–28.00 EUR (minPrice/maxPrice in cents; priceRange text "De 10 à 28 €")
price.notes: Each API event resource's own 'minPrice'/'maxPrice' (integer cents) and human-readable 'priceRange' string, stated directly.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from a self-consistent retained artifact (JSON-LD Organization address exactly matching the task-given address; every API record's own placesNames confirms the same venue name).

acquisition_class PUBLIC_JSON_API, a resolved supported class, reached via Level 1 (INSUFFICIENT — the query-string genre filter is not honoured server-side) then Level 2 (SUFFICIENT — the Nuxt frontend's own public, self-documenting Hydra API, correctly filterable once the right parameter names and tag IRI were resolved).
CONFIRMED public data paths retained: the filtered /api/events collection (concert tag + future dates) and the /api/tags lookup used to resolve the tag IRI.

title, start_date, time, end, venue_location, source_record_id, and event_url all PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE; price additionally PROVEN — a genuinely complete field set, better than most sources in this project's prior Berlin/Barcelona trials.

source_record_id PROVEN via the API's own documented, stable Hydra resource IRI ('@id') — a stronger identity guarantee than a URL-slug fallback, since it is the source's own explicit resource identity scheme.

No existing collector family/module in this repository implements a Hydra/API-Platform-style JSON API (ingestion/events-calendar-api/ is specific to the WordPress Tribe Events Calendar REST shape, a different vocabulary and pagination model). recommended_family is the existing generic 'JSON_API' vocabulary member (COLLECTOR_FAMILIES), but its concrete implementation for this source is genuinely new code (ingestion/centquatre-paris/).

DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION offline-proof evidence now retained (tests/centquatre-paris.test.mjs), re-parsing the retained fixture via the new ingestion/centquatre-paris/ adapter and reproducing the exact claimed field values deterministically.

No unresolved CRITICAL blocker. READY_FOR_ACTIVATION was deliberately not claimed; turning this into an enabled source is a separate, later, explicitly-authorised step outside this investigation's scope.

One honest caveat: the task-given events URL's own '?genre=concerts' query parameter has no server-side effect — any future activation must call the /api/events endpoint directly with the documented taggedEntities.tag[] filter, not rely on that query string.
